classification.difficultyReason: Construct two representations of a two-stage sample space and count outcomes satisfying compound conditions.

content.prompt: A die is rolled and a coin is tossed. The pair of results is written down.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Draw a tree diagram for the experiment.

answer.short: Six branches labelled 1–6, each splitting into H and T.
answer.worked: Each die result branches to H (head) and T (tail), giving 12 possible paths.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 9a; teacher PDF page 40, Review exercise 9a
spec.description: Six first-stage die branches, each followed by the two coin outcomes.
spec.mathematics: Six die outcomes each have two coin outcomes, producing twelve paths.
spec.answerVisibility: Solution only; student receives an unfilled drawing area.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Draw an array diagram for the experiment.

inlines.text: Use columns for die results 1–6 and rows for H and T. Each cell records (coin result, die result), giving the following 12 outcomes.

children.label: c
children.prompt: What is the probability of obtaining a tail and a 5?

answer.worked:
The only favourable outcome is $(T,5)$, out of 12 equally likely outcomes.
$$P(\text{tail and 5})=\frac{1}{12}.$$

children.label: d
children.prompt: List the favourable outcomes for the event ‘obtain a head following an even number’.

answer.worked: The even die results are 2, 4 and 6. Pair each with H: $(H,2),\ (H,4),\ (H,6)$, where each pair records (coin result, die result).

children.label: e
children.prompt: What is the probability of obtaining a head following an even number?

answer.worked:
There are 3 favourable outcomes among the 12 equally likely outcomes.
$$\begin{align*}P(\text{head following an even number})&=\frac{3}{12}\\P(\text{head following an even number})&=\frac14.\end{align*}$$

children.label: f
children.prompt: What is the probability of obtaining a tail and a number greater than 3?

answer.worked:
The favourable outcomes are $(T,4),\ (T,5),\ (T,6)$, among 12 equally likely outcomes.
$$\begin{align*}P(\text{tail and number greater than 3})&=\frac{3}{12}\\P(\text{tail and number greater than 3})&=\frac14.\end{align*}$$
